lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A lawyer tested Jesus with a question. He answered with a road.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Crowds followed Jesus everywhere, and this man wanted to catch him out.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A lawyer is a man who knows the rules. He wanted to know exactly where they stopped.

lines.speaker: Lawyer
lines.text: Teacher, the law says to love my neighbour. But who is my neighbour?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He wanted a short list. A line to draw, with some people on each side.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Jesus did not give him a list. He told him a story.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: It is a parable Jesus told, and it begins on a very lonely road.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A man was walking from Jerusalem down to Jericho. It was a long, steep road, and a dangerous one.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The hills hid robbers, and travellers there kept their eyes open and their bags close.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: This man walked alone. He was tired, and he was not thinking about danger.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The sun was high and the road was empty, and the heat shimmered on the stones.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Then, in a bend of the road, the robbers stepped out.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: When they were gone, the road was quiet. The man lay by the side of it, and his bag was gone.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He could not stand. He could not call out. He could only wait for someone to come.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The first to come was a priest. A respected man, with an important place to be.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He saw the man lying there. And he crossed to the other side of the road.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Maybe he was late. Maybe he was afraid. Maybe he told himself someone else would help.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He walked on. His steps got faster, not slower.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Then came a Levite, a man who served in the temple. He came close enough to look.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He looked. And he, too, crossed to the other side.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Two good men, two good reasons, and one man still lying on the road.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The road was empty again, except for the dust, and one man waiting.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The third traveller was a Samaritan. The people listening to Jesus looked down on Samaritans.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He had every reason to keep walking. He did not.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He did not ask who the man was. He did not ask where he came from.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He stopped. He knelt in the dust beside the stranger.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The robbers might still be close. He knelt there anyway.

lines.speaker: Samaritan
lines.text: Hold on, friend. You are not alone now.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He cleaned and bandaged him, using the oil and wine he carried for his own journey.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Then he lifted him onto his own donkey, and walked beside him, one slow step at a time.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: It cost him time, and it cost him money. He did not count either.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They reached an inn as the sun went down. The Samaritan did not leave him at the door.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He carried the man in, found him a bed, and stayed with him all night.

lines.speaker: Samaritan
lines.text: Is there a room? He needs rest, and food, and someone to watch over him.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: All night he stayed by the bed, changing the bandages by lamplight.

lines.speaker: Innkeeper
lines.text: There is. But a room costs money, friend. Who is going to pay for it?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The Samaritan nodded. He had already thought of that.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: In the morning, the Samaritan had to go. But he did not just walk away.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He took out two silver coins, and put them in the innkeeper's hand.

lines.speaker: Samaritan
lines.text: Look after him. If it costs more, I will pay you when I come back.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He did not ask the man his name. He did not ask what he believed.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Then he went on his way, and the innkeeper looked after the stranger.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He saw a man who needed help, and he was the one standing there.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Jesus looked at the lawyer, and asked him one question.

lines.speaker: Jesus
lines.text: Which of these three was a neighbour to the man the robbers left on the road?

lines.speaker: Lawyer
lines.text: The one who showed him mercy.

lines.speaker: Jesus
lines.text: Go, and do the same.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The lawyer said nothing for a long moment. Everyone listening knew who had stopped.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The lawyer had asked who counts as a neighbour. Jesus turned the question around.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Not, who deserves my help? But, will I be the one who stops?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Jesus did not tell him who to help. He told him who to become.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Everyone has a road like that. And everyone has someone lying beside it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Who is on the other side of your road this week?
